newsitem.title: VIETNAM: ICO mulls coffee promotion in China, Russia.
newsitem.headline: ICO mulls coffee promotion in China, Russia.

text.p: The International Coffee Organisation (ICO) said on Tuesday it is mulling tactics to promote consumption of coffee in China and Russia while risk management will become increasingly important to the trade.

"The ICO Promotion Committee is presently considering the tactics to be employed in promoting the consumption of coffee in China and Russia," ICO Executive Director Celsius Lodder said at the Third Asia International Coffee Conference here.
"If these markets can be developed, the benefits to coffee producers, in all countries, will be immense," Lodder said in remarks read for him by another ICO official.
The two countries represent the "Holy Grail" of the coffee business because increasing consumption in these big potential markets would provide a fundamental fillip to currently weak coffee prices.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said late last month that it estimated 1996/97 world green coffee output would 100.9 million 60-kilogram bags, up 1.8 million from its estimate of 99.1 million in June 1996.
Soft prices have prompted African coffee producers to call for a reduction in exports in the first half of 1997 in a bid to bolster the market.

Lodder said the purchase and sale of coffee derivatives, swaps, commodity bonds and other financial instruments for risk management "will become...even more important for exporters, traders and roasters."
"(They) may replace stocks and other fundamental factors as the major driving force in market price determination in the short and medium term," he said.

"The coffee market is now exhibiting the same type of development that has recently occurred in both financial markets and manufacturing industry," the ICO official added. "Inevitably, changes will have a negative effect on some individuals, firms and sectors of the market."
